OSAGE BEACH, Mo., Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What does it mean to build a home at the Lake of the Ozarks with intention? That question is answered in a HelloNation article featuring advice from Custom Home Builder Expert Cole Glascock of Glascock Construction in Osage Beach, Missouri. The article outlines how thoughtful planning and flexible home design can help homeowners create lake properties that serve both current needs and long-term goals. The article explains that many Lake of the Ozarks homes begin as weekend getaways or seasonal retreats but often transition into full-time residences. Designing with that future in mind helps ensure the home can adapt over time. According to the article, intentional planning supports a balance between entertainment, relaxation, and privacy, which are all central to the lake lifestyle. A key focus of the article is floor plan design. It outlines how flexible rooms, open living spaces, and seamless indoor-outdoor connections allow for multi-purpose use. Whether a space is used today as a game room or gym, it can later serve as a guest suite or home office if planned correctly. The article notes that placing full bathrooms near these areas improves functionality and supports future resale value. The article emphasizes the importance of an experienced custom home

items.title: Developer Shares His Vision — And Images — For The Future Of Regalia Hotel In Lake Ozark
items.desc: There has been a lot of buzz, excitement and speculation regarding the planned “Summit Resort & Sports Complex,” so I thought I’d try to give an update, and provide some context, background and perspective about the proposed project.
items.body: There has been a lot of buzz, excitement and speculation regarding the planned “Summit Resort & Sports Complex,” so I thought I’d try to give an update, and provide some context, background and perspective about the proposed project. This past spring, I was contacted by the lender of the Regalia hotel property and assisted them initially as a consultant. The property was foreclosed on in early July, at which point I agreed to proceed with the lender group as a co-owner, and managing partner; if, we were to proceed with extensive renovations, to include a complete facelift of the building, major renovations throughout, including both the indoor and outdoor swimming pools, fitness center, new spa, and other improvements and additions necessary to transform the property into a modern, five star luxury resort. Part of these renovations will include transforming the old indoor tennis court facility into a modern multi-purpose sports court. The property currently only has 83 rooms, which is not an adequate number of rooms to allow this property to succeed, which has always been a challenging factor. Our plan will add another 128 guest rooms, for a total room count of 211. Phase three of our project will include building a new indoor and outdoor sports complex; primarily focused on pickle ball, which is the fastest growing sport in the US today. Our primary focus and marketing strategy will be the “Sports Tourism” market, with a world class hotel and sports facility that will attract youth and adult sports tournaments and camps for everything including; volleyball, basketball, gymnastics, dance, cheerleading, wrestling, martial arts, and the list is endless. This will be a fantastic addition for the entire Lake of the Ozarks community, and a tremendous boom to economic develop

items.title: Marshfield Community Theatre Presents: Carrie: The Musical This Halloween
items.desc: This Halloween season, the Marshfield Community Theatre is bringing you something old and something new. “We are currently producing Carrie: The Musical, based on the iconic story by Stephen King,” […]
items.body: This Halloween season, the Marshfield Community Theatre is bringing you something old and something new. “We are currently producing Carrie: The Musical, based on the iconic story by Stephen King,” shared an excited Kelby Lorenz, Director of Carrie and Director of Outreach for Marshfield Community Theatre. “We chose this show because it’s October; we are doing it Halloween weekend. It seemed like a really good spooky show, but when I read the script, it tells a really incredible story,” reflected Lorenz. “One of the things that I love about this show and the way that it’s interpreted is that it’s a closed loop-we end where we start. We got to really play with the idea of how long have we been stuck in this loop…and how long have we been trying to stop the destruction.” “It’s a cool concept to play with-around the idea of trauma, how it stays with us…and how traumatic moments can really impact the way we interact with each other,” expressed Lorenz. “It really centers on that theme-what does it cost to be kind?” The cast includes around 16, with most actors new to MCT, including a mix of MSU students and brand-new actors. The production team includes Lorenz as Director, Nico Jenkins as Assistant Director, Linley Wilson as Music Director, Miliani Kloster as Choreographer, and Toni Lorenz as Production Manager. “It’s been super fun,” shared Lauren Knight, a Missouri State student playing Carrie White. “I haven’t done a lot of roles where I’m a lead- it’s been a bit of a change. It’s been fun to get to know this character. She’s been a bit of a challenge…I’ve learned to be more vulnerable on stage. items.title: Lake Of The Ozarks Resort Mogul Has Big Plans To Buy, Renovate Foreclosed Regalia Hotel
items.desc: LAKE OZARK, Mo. — It's been eerily quiet at The Regalia Hotel this year. But that's about to change.
items.body: LAKE OZARK, Mo. — It's been eerily quiet at The Regalia Hotel this year. But that's about to change. After a short run at Lake of the Ozarks, the hotel and conference center closed and was foreclosed on, in the past year. It appeared without fanfare in an online real estate auction in 2023, with bidding approaching $3 million, though it's not clear that the resort changed hands at that time. This year's closure happened quietly, catching many visitors by surprise. On May 25, one person posted in a local Facebook group, "We booked a room at the Regalia Hotel on Horseshoe Bend for Memorial Day weekend, and we tried calling several times, but the phones were disconnected. We pulled up to an empty parking lot, overgrown grass and the front doors were locked. Did this place permanently close or awaiting new owners?" Turns out, it was awaiting a new owner. Developer Merlyn Vandervort has confirmed to LakeExpo that he is in the process of purchasing The Regalia, with plans to fully renovate the property, rebranding it The Summit. When operating, The Regalia had 83 rooms. Vandervort plans to more than double that number. Rezoning for the property was approved by the Camden County Commission on Thursday, Oct. 22, after receiving unanimous recommendation from the Planning & Zoning Commission. "I have not taken ownership of the property yet, the rezoning was one of the things that had to get completed first," Vandervort confirmed in an email on Oct. 13. "Now it’s a matter of working a deal out with the current lender who foreclosed on the property." On Friday, Vandervort said with the rezoning approved, "Now the tough work begins." items.title: Athlete of the Week: Johnny Carriger, Crocker Soccer
items.desc: Share on Facebook Share on Twitter As an underclassman, Johnny Carriger was ready for the moment, scoring a hat trick in Crocker’s district championship game. “I think we just wanted it more,” Johnny said. “They came out
items.body: As an underclassman, Johnny Carriger was ready for the moment, scoring a hat trick in Crocker’s district championship game. “I think we just wanted it more,” Johnny said. “They came out like they were going to win. They went up 2-0 in the first half, and I was like someone’s got to step up. So I did.” It was his second hat trick of the tournament, all while battling illness and injury. “He had a 103 fever at district time to send us to the final,” said Crocker Head Soccer Coach Rich Heenan. “Two weeks prior he had broke his hand and powered through without anything on his hand. [Johnny] played the rest of the season in a full cast.” On top of toughness, scoring goals runs in the family. His older brother, Tristen, put up Laquey’s lone goal in the Hornet’s state semifinal game. Johnny was there watching in the stands. “Whenever he scored it I was like dang, why couldn’t that be me,” Johnny said. Now, Tristen is Crocker’s assistant soccer coach. “I just cannot call him coach,” Johnny said. “It’s just too funny.” “He’s watched me play for years,” Tristen Carriger said. “But now it’s me watching him play.” Johnny is nearing 100 career goals as a varsity starter. 34 of them are in the last 16 games. Tristen gets a front-row view of his brother’s success and more. “He likes to help his teammates and help them figure out how to pass the ball better [or] how to do a soccer move,” Tristen said. “[He] even leads them to getting their first goal.” Johnny has no plans of slowing his scoring spree, but as his brother would wan, he’s turned into a leader on top of a striker.

items.body: On Saturday, September 26, 2026, at noon, the Class of 1972 held its 54th Class Reunion at the Riddick Masonic Lodge in Buffalo. We enjoyed a bountiful potluck dinner and great conversations with our classmates. There were 17 classmates in attendance. We missed those that couldn’t be there this year, and we set a date for our 55th Class Reunion to be held on Saturday, September 25, 2027, at the Riddick Masonic Lodge. We hope to see everyone next year.

items.title: Sunshine Club learns history at October meeting
items.desc: The Fair Grove Sunshine Club met October 14th at the Fair Grove Senior Center. The members attending were Evelyn Kerby, Marilyn Smith, Robbie Gillet, Holly Barlow, Lynda Hutchison, Carolyn Riggi, […]
items.body: The Fair Grove Sunshine Club met October 14th at the Fair Grove Senior Center. The members attending were Evelyn Kerby, Marilyn Smith, Robbie Gillet, Holly Barlow, Lynda Hutchison, Carolyn Riggi, Mary Terry, Peggy Schletty, Rue Withers, Toni Woffard, Ellen Carter, Pam Meyers & Carol Highfill. Everyone had lunch and the Business Meeting followed. Marilyn Smith gave the History of the Sunshine Club. It was started as the W.P.F.A Club in 1923 which stands for the Women’s Progressive Farmer’s Association. When it disbanded in 1986, the Club wanted to continue on, so it was named the Sunshine Club. The Club has met every month for 103 years. The Club has met in everyone’s homes, and went to many interesting places all over the area. We have toured many educational places and always looked forward to the good meals we have shared in homes, Tea Rooms, Restaurants, and the Senior Center. New members are always welcomed.

items.body: Warm up with a delicious meal and support a great cause! The community is invited to the CWF’s Chili & Soup Luncheon on Wednesday, November 4th from 11:00 AM to 1:30 PM. The event will be held at the Buffalo First Christian Church, located at 502 N. Maple St., Buffalo, MO. In addition to a variety of hot chilis and soups, attendees can browse a homemade bake sale and enjoy a beautiful quilt show showcasing local talent. Admission is by donation only, and carry-out options are available for those on the go. Come out for great food, beautiful quilts, and wonderful community fellowship!
